text: If the Sun vanished right now, you wouldn't know for eight minutes.
That's how long sunlight takes to reach us. The last of it is still on its way.
And Earth would keep circling nothing, because gravity travels at the speed of light too.
Then, at eight minutes and twenty seconds, the lights go out.
And Earth flies off in a straight line, at thirty kilometres a second.
The Moon comes with us. Earth's gravity still holds it.
The Moon goes dark too. But Jupiter keeps shining for over an hour.
Without sunlight, plants stop making food.
Within a week, it's about minus eighteen degrees, on average.
Within a year, about minus seventy. The oceans freeze over.
But the ice works like a blanket. Underneath, the deep ocean stays liquid, warmed from below.
And down at the hot vents, life that never needed the Sun keeps going.
The good news: the Sun can't just vanish. All that mass has to go somewhere.
So relax. The sunlight on your face right now left the Sun eight minutes ago.
